The HRP fitness and bone evidence reports address reduced cardiorespiratory and musculoskeletal fitness and fracture risk associated with spaceflight-related bone changes. These reports provide research context, not a user-specific exercise or rehabilitation plan. ASTHRAL provides project-authored generic movement examples to support a manual software workflow; they are not NASA training protocol content, approved mission countermeasures, or individualized prescriptions. The user records activity, workload, sets, repetitions and time. The app does not estimate VO2, strength, bone density, injury risk, form or readiness.

Existing reference outlines discuss authorized exercise or mission countermeasure plans; ASTHRAL does not generate an exercise prescription, assume equipment availability, or replace mission review. DXA and laboratory capability are not assumed available in flight. Standing-test interpretations cannot be transferred automatically to free microgravity. Recovery and follow-up require the appropriate gravity context and comparable measurements. ## Sleep, fatigue, cognition, immune markers, and radiation Recorded sleep duration, sleep efficiency, fatigue scales, reaction-time tests, viral measurements, and radiation records require their original methods, units, timing, and context. A fatigue score must match its declared scale. A PCR trend alone is not a reactivation diagnosis. Dosimetric exposure is not a cancer diagnosis, and a recorded interval total is not a lifetime dose.
